Usage: [command] [-h|--help] [--version]

Commands:
  batch        Run one compact ranking query across up to 24 cases in a capture manifest.
  cache        Build, reuse, or remove the ETLX conversion cache beside a trace.
  callers      Report the immediate CPU callers of a frame; the drill-down after a CPU ranking.
  classify     Summarize CPU self-time by runtime work category - zeroing, copying, GC,
      write-barrier, JIT, or other - answering "where did the time go: zeroing memory?
      copying strings? in the GC?". Pair with --native-symbols so the native runtime
      work resolves; without it the native leaves fall in 'other'.
  collect      Record a Windows ETW (.etl) trace of a launched executable, then print the analysis
      commands the capture unlocks. Windows-only and requires Administrator; for an
      EventPipe (.nettrace) capture use dotnet-trace (cross-platform).
  diff         Compare two like-for-like CPU traces or capture manifests by absolute and normalized sampled-time change.
  events       Query the trace's raw events by name, with paging and a per-event payload cap.
  export       Export a trace to a flame-graph file for speedscope or chrome://tracing.
  info         Report a trace's identity and quality signals - the orientation step to run first.
  lifecycle    Report where a command's wall clock went: per-invocation root lifetime, time to
      the first child, child span, and teardown, with p50/min/max across invocations.
  processes    List the processes in a trace, ranked by CPU-sample weight, so a multi-process
      capture can be scoped to the right one with the --process option on the other
      verbs.
  rank         Rank the hottest frames in a trace by self or inclusive metric weight.
  report       Run a bounded structured runtime or operating-system report.
  source       Inspect CPU source attribution as ranked lines or a per-file heat map.
  timeline     Correlate trace activity as aligned time buckets or a bounded snapshot around one millisecond.
  tree         Sh

Usage: batch [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Run one compact ranking query across up to 24 cases in a capture manifest.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Path to a capture helper manifest.json.

Options:
  --metric <string>          Provider metric: cpu, threadtime, alloc, exceptions, contention, wait, or activity. [Default: @"cpu"]
  -m, --measure <Measure>    self or inclusive. [Default: Self]
  --root <string>            Optional root frame applied to every case. [Default: @""]
  --fold <string[]?>         Extra leaf-frame fold regexes; omit for defaults. [Default: null]
  --symbols <string?>        Optional symbol directory overriding each case's recorded directory. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when any loaded case has poor symbol resolution.
  --process <string>         Process substring overriding the manifest process. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process rather than manifest/automatic scope.
  --pid <int[]?>             Scope to these exact process ids (comma-separated); excludes --process and --all-processes. [Default: null]
  --children <Children>      Whether the process scope follows descendants: include (default) or exclude. [Default: Include]
  --benchmark                Use the BenchmarkDotNet measured-workload root.

Report the immediate CPU callers of a frame; the drill-down after a CPU ranking.

Options:
  --root <string>            Substring scoping the analysis to the subtree under a frame. [Default: @""]

  -s, --symbols <string?>    Build-output directory whose PDBs map managed code to source lines. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when symbol resolution is below the trusted threshold.
  --process <string>         Scope to the process tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope to the busiest. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process instead of auto-scoping to the busiest (multi-process captures).
  --pid <int[]?>             Scope to these exact process ids (comma-separated); excludes --process and --all-processes. [Default: null]
  --children <Children>      Whether the process scope follows descendants: include (default) or exclude. [Default: Include]
  --benchmark                Scope to the BenchmarkDotNet measured-workload subtree (preset root); for BDN captures.
  --callees                  Also report the focus frame's immediate callees (a caller/callee view).

      work resolves; without it the native leaves fall in 'other'.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Path to a .speedscope.json, .nettrace, or .etl file.

Options:
  --root <string>            Substring scoping the classification to the subtree under a frame. [Default: @""]
  -s, --symbols <string?>    Build-output directory whose PDBs map managed code to source lines. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when symbol resolution is below the trusted threshold.
  --process <string>         Scope to the process tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope to the busiest. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process instead of auto-scoping to the busiest (multi-process captures).
  --pid <int[]?>             Scope to these exact process ids (comma-separated); excludes --process and --all-processes. [Default: null]
  --children <Children>      Whether the process scope follows descendants: include (default) or exclude. [Default: Include]

result.stdout:
Usage: collect [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Record a Windows ETW (.etl) trace of a launched executable, then print the analysis
      commands the capture unlocks. Windows-only and requires Administrator; for an
      EventPipe (.nettrace) capture use dotnet-trace (cross-platform).

Options:
  --launch <string>          Path to the executable to launch and trace (the built app, never 'dotnet run'). [Required]
  --output <string>          Path of the .etl file to write. [Required]
  --profile <string>         Providers to enable: cpu (default), threadtime (adds context switches for wall-clock time), or startup (low-perturbation; only the CLR keywords that name managed methods). [Default: @"cpu"]
  --launch-args <string>     Arguments passed to the launched executable, as one command-line string. [Default: @""]
  --cpu-ms <double>          CPU sample interval in milliseconds; sub-millisecond is what makes a 30-100 ms command rankable. Clamped to the range this machine reports as honored, and a clamp is reported with that range. [Default: 1]
  --duration <int>           Optional cap on capture length in seconds, applied to each launch; 0 (default) waits for each to exit. [Default: 0]
  --iterations <int>         How many times to launch the executable inside the one session. Amortizes session startup over a short command, which is otherwise mostly capture overhead. [Default: 1]
  --max-size-mb <int>        Optional cap on the capture's on-disk size in megabytes; 0 (default) writes an unbounded file. When set, a circular buffer keeps the last N MB - size it to hold the run, since a full ring overwrites the oldest events and can drop early JIT method names. [Default: 0]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]

Usage: diff [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Compare two like-for-like CPU traces or capture manifests by absolute and normalized sampled-time change.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Baseline trace or capture manifest.json.
  [1] <string>    Current trace or capture manifest.json; both inputs must have the same kind.

Options:
  -m, --measure <Measure>    Which measure to compare: self (leaf time, helpers folded) or inclusive. [Default: Self]
  --root <string>            Substring scoping both rankings to the subtree under a frame. [Default: @""]
  -n, --top <int>            Maximum number of changed rows to return. [Default: 25]
  --fold <string[]?>         Extra leaf-frame fold regexes (comma-separated); omit to use the built-in defaults. [Default: null]
  -s, --symbols <string?>    Build-output directory whose PDBs map managed code to source lines. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when either trace's symbol resolution is below the trusted threshold.
  --process <string>         Scope both traces to the process tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process in both traces instead of auto-scoping.
  --pid <int[]?>             Scope both traces to these exact process ids (comma-separated); excludes --process and --all-processes. [Default: null]
  --children <Children>      Whether the process scope follows descendants: include (default) or exclude. [Default: Include]
  --benchmark                Scope both traces to the BenchmarkDotNet measured-workload subtree.

Arguments:

  --name <string>            Case-insensitive substring matched against provider/event; omit to match every event. [Default: @""]
  --skip <int>               Number of matches to skip, for paging. [Default: 0]
  -n, --take <int>           Maximum matches to return; 0 returns only the total count. [Default: 50]
  --max-payload <int>        Per-event payload character cap; 0 omits payloads. [Default: 200]
  --payload <string>         Keep only events whose payload values contain this (case-insensitive); omit for no payload filter. [Default: @""]
  --pid <int>                Keep only events from this process id; omit for every process. [Default: -1]
  --tid <int>                Keep only events on this thread id; omit for every thread. [Default: -1]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]

Usage: timeline [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Correlate trace activity as aligned time buckets or a bounded snapshot around one millisecond.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Path to a .nettrace EventPipe or .etl ETW file (a speedscope export is rejected).

Options:
  --mode <TimelineMode>      View to return: buckets (default) or snapshot. [Default: Buckets]
  --at <double?>             Snapshot center in 0.01 ms increments relative to trace start; required for snapshot. [Default: null]
  --window <double?>         Half-window in 0.01 ms increments on either side of --at; defaults to 100 (snapshot only). [Default: null]
  --lanes <string>           Bucket-mode lanes: gc, cpu, exceptions, alloc, jit; omit for every lane. [Default: @""]
  -n, --buckets <int?>       Bucket-mode slice count; defaults to 50 (clamped to 5-200). [Default: null]
  --time <string>            Bucket-mode time window 'start,end' in ms; either bound may be omitted. [Default: @""]
  --process <string>         Scope a multi-process .etl to the tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope to the busiest. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process instead of auto-scoping to the busiest (multi-process captures).
  --pid <int[]?>             Scope to these exact process ids (comma-separated); excludes --process and --all-processes. [Default: null]
  --children <Children>      Whether the process scope follows descendants: include (default) or exclude. [Default: Include]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]

Usage: tree [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Show the top-down CPU call tree, following the hot path from the root into its callees.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Path to a .speedscope.json, .nettrace, or .etl file.

Options:
  --root <string>            Substring scoping the tree to the subtree under a frame. [Default: @""]
  -d, --max-depth <int>      Maximum number of frame levels to expand below the root. [Default: 10]
  --min-pct <double>         Minimum share of the scoped total (percent) a node must have to appear; 0 shows all. [Default: 1]
  --fold <string[]?>         Extra leaf-frame fold regexes (comma-separated); omit to use the built-in defaults. [Default: null]
  -s, --symbols <string?>    Build-output directory whose PDBs map managed code to source lines. [Default: null]
  --format <OutputFormat>    Render format: text or json. [Default: Text]
  --strict                   Exit 3 when symbol resolution is below the trusted threshold.
  --process <string>         Scope to the process tree whose name contains this; omit to auto-scope to the busiest. [Default: @""]
  --all-processes            Read every process instead of auto-scoping to the busiest (multi-process captures).
  --pid <int[]?>             Scope to these exact process ids (comma-separated); excludes --process and --all-processes. [Default: null]
  --children <Children>      Whether the process scope follows descendants: include (default) or exclude. [Default: Include]
  --benchmark                Scope to the BenchmarkDotNet measured-workload subtree (preset root); for BDN captures.
